comments.text: Entry from the loader (jmp $0400 once OVL1 is in). Masks every CIA interrupt, points the NMI vector at $17DA, sets the video bank and chip registers, copies $FF00-$FFFF to $0200, silences the SID through $E0DE and seeds the game's variables.

Each pass of the main loop: with Z, A, C, H and 1 all held, writes $60 (rts) over the first byte of $2BC8, so that check returns at once; with N held, writes $EA (nop) back. Tested live on 7 October 2026: holding the five keys in the jungle changed $2BC8 from $EA to $60.
Tests F1, F3, F5 and F7 through $BA6A and calls $BFB8 for each one held; the manual's switch between platoon members.
With $F173 clear, RUN/STOP held drops this call's return and jumps to $A709.
Reads control port 2 ($DC00) into $0306 for the soldier's movement.
Reads row 7 of the keyboard; with SPACE held, a grenade left ($BD55 non-zero) and $1E1B clear, calls $BD31 and starts the throw.
NMI handler. When CIA 2 raised it (bit 7 of $DD0D), acknowledges it and sets $1A11 to 1; any other NMI, such as RESTORE, jumps to $0108 in the stack page.

First of the ten raster interrupt handlers of the play screen, about line 20. Saves the registers, banks I/O in, sets the scroll registers from $0303 and $18BF, names $18C1 as the next handler, then sets up the sprites for the top of the screen: enable, priority, expansion, X high bits, the positions of sprites 0 to 2 and the pointers at $43F8 and $47F8 (lines 20 to 30 in a recorded frame). The handlers chain through $FFFE, each naming the next: $17FE, $18C1, $1916, $1966, $1A12, $1A8A, $1ACA, $1B12, $1B63, $1C2E, and back to $17FE.
Second handler of the play screen's chain. In a recorded frame its only video write named $1916 as the next handler, at line 136; what else it does is open.
Third handler of the play screen's chain: puts every sprite behind the background ($D01B = $FF, line 146 in a recorded frame) and names $1966.
Fourth handler of the play screen's chain: moves sprite 0 and changes its pointer and colour (line 150 in a recorded frame), then names $1A12.
Fifth handler of the play screen's chain, at the foot of the play area: moves sprites 0 to 2 off, turns every sprite off and changes $D016 (lines 195 and 196 in a recorded frame).
Sixth handler of the play screen's chain: sets $D018 to 1 and $D016 to 198 for the status panel (line 202 in a recorded frame).
Seventh handler of the play screen's chain: sets $D018 to 3 and $D016 to 200 (line 210 in a recorded frame).
Eighth handler of the play screen's chain: sets the border and background to light grey (line 213 in a recorded frame), then names $1B63.
Ninth handler of the play screen's chain: sets the border and background back to black (line 216 in a recorded frame); $1C2E was named next at line 249.
Last handler of the play screen's chain; it names $17FE as the next, written at line 5 of the following frame.
The interrupt handler the vector held on the title screen.
Reads two keys: P (row 5, column 1) sets $0C85 to 1, G (row 3, column 2) clears it. What $0C85 does is open; the manual's pause is the likely reading, not yet tested.

Compares the soldier's position ($0C73, $0C7B) with each entry of a list at $0C74 and $0C7C indexed by X (most likely the enemies), inside 20 by 6, and on a match goes to $2CB7. The ZACH1 key cheat at $07B5 turns its first byte into rts; what $2CB7 does is open.
Screen messages in PETSCII: THE FIRST CASUALTY OF WAR IS INNOCENCE, ENTERING THE COMBAT ZONE, GAME OVER, TEN BEST SCORES, ENTER YOUR NAME.

Is key A held? A is the KERNAL's key number (eight times the row plus the column); the row's select byte comes from $BAA6 and the column's mask from $BAAE. Returns carry set when held. Called from 23 places.
Eight row-select bytes for $DC00, $FE to $7F, indexed by the key number divided by 8.
Eight column masks for $DC01, $01 to $80, indexed by the key number's low three bits.
Takes one grenade: decrements the count at $BD55 and blanks its icon in the status panel at $4398 plus the count.
Grenades the soldier has left; $BD31 takes one.

The messages of the jungle and village, 40 characters each in PETSCII: what a search finds (a sack of flour, a pot of rice, a torch, the explosives, a trapdoor), the bridge, the booby trap, the warning about villagers, and TURN THE DISK OVER TO SIDE B.
Clears the music driver's state and every SID register $D400-$D417, then sets the volume to 15.
Starts sound effect A on voice X: copies its three parameters from the tables at $F07A, $F08C and $F09E into the voice's slots. Called from 24 places in the game.
The ten high scores the game starts with, PLATOON 199998 down to 009145, copied to $0200 by $0400 at the start.
